# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply (high confidence). However, following the "AI Omnibus" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this date has been pushed back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A small set of uncorroborated blog sources claim a further delay to 2 August 2029, but this is not confirmed by any official EU source and should be treated with significant skepticism.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Framework (Pre-Amendment)
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were to become subject to obligations 36 months after entry into force, corresponding to 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). Article 113(c) of the original text specifically provided that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III high-risk systems) would apply from this date (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay application of high-risk rules by up to 16 months, conditioning the start date on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools are available (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). This proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement was reached between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and the amendment entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Applicable Date
As amended by the AI Omnibus (in force 27 July 2026), obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), confirmed by multiple official EU Commission sources including the AI Act Service Desk and Digital Strategy pages ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force); [Timeline Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). No specific regulation number for this amendment appears in the available sources; it is referred to only as the "AI Omnibus" or "Digital Omnibus on AI." Separately, high-risk AI systems that are safety components of regulated products under Annex I apply from a later date, 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Related Provisions
Under the consolidated text as of 27 July 2026, Article 111(2) provides that already-placed-on-market high-risk systems become subject to the Regulation only if they undergo significant design changes after 2 August 2026, referencing the Chapter III application date in Article 113 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Service Desk Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). It is unclear whether this cross-reference has been updated to reflect the new 2 December 2027 date. Other AI Act obligations—prohibitions on certain practices, AI literacy requirements, and GPAI/governance rules—apply on different, earlier timelines than the Annex III high-risk rules (high confidence) ([Timeline Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act); [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several uncorroborated sources ([responsibleailabs.ai](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, apparently reflecting the pre-Omnibus text and not updated to reflect the later amendment.

A set of three news-blog sources (low confidence, flagged below 0.4) claim a "final text agreed in September 2026" further delayed the deadline to 2 August 2029 ([eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update), [ai-law-insights.example](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply), [tech-legal-alerts.example](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline)). No official EU Commission, Council, or EUR-Lex source corroborates this claim, and these sources lack clear authority or verifiable publication provenance. This should be treated as unconfirmed and potentially inaccurate.

## Knowledge Gaps
- No official source confirms or denies the alleged 2 August 2029 delay; it is unclear whether such an amendment exists or was legitimately adopted through ordinary legislative procedure.
- The precise legal citation (regulation number) for the AI Omnibus amendment is not specified in any available source, nor is it clear whether Article 111(2)/113 cross-references have been formally updated to point to 2 December 2027 rather than 2 August 2026.
- The full legal text of any "second amendment" allegedly agreed in September 2026 has not been located or verified.
- It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date applies uniformly across all Annex III categories or whether sub-exceptions exist (e.g., under Article 6(5) reclassification mechanisms).

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would apply (high confidence). However, following the "AI Omnibus" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, this date has been pushed back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A small set of uncorroborated blog sources claim a further delay to 2 August 2029, but this is not confirmed by any official EU source and should be treated with significant skepticism.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Framework (Pre-Amendment)
Under the AI Act as adopted in 2024, high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were to become subject to obligations 36 months after entry into force, corresponding to 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline); [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). Article 113(c) of the original text specifically provided that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III high-risk systems) would apply from this date (medium confidence) ([ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113); [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission proposed a "Digital Omnibus on AI" to delay application of high-risk rules by up to 16 months, conditioning the start date on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools are available (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules); [Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). This proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, political agreement was reached between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, and the amendment entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai); [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Applicable Date
As amended, Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), confirmed by multiple official EU Commission sources including the AI Act Service Desk and Digital Strategy pages ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force); [Timeline Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)). Separately, high-risk AI systems that are safety components of regulated products under Annex I apply from a later date, 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation); [Digital Strategy FAQ](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Related Provisions
Under the consolidated text as of 27 July 2026, Article 111(2) provides that already-placed-on-market high-risk systems become subject to the Regulation only if they undergo significant design changes after 2 August 2026, referencing the Chapter III application date in Article 113 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727); [AI Act Service Desk Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Other AI Act obligations—prohibitions on certain practices, AI literacy requirements, and GPAI/governance rules—apply on different, earlier timelines than the Annex III high-risk rules (high confidence) ([Timeline Implementation](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act); [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several uncorroborated sources ([responsibleailabs.ai](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)) still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, apparently reflecting the pre-Omnibus text and not updated to reflect the later amendment.

A set of three news-blog sources (low confidence, flagged below 0.4) claim a "final text agreed in September 2026" further delayed the deadline to 2 August 2029 ([eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update); [ai-law-insights.example](https://ai-law-insights.example/2026/09/22/when-do-annex-iii-rules-apply); [tech-legal-alerts.example](https://tech-legal-alerts.example/2026-09-29-ai-act-high-risk-timeline)). No official EU Commission, Council, or EUR-Lex source corroborates this claim, and these sources lack clear authority or verifiable publication provenance. This should be treated as unconfirmed and potentially inaccurate.

## Knowledge Gaps
- No official source confirms or denies the alleged 2 August 2029 delay; it is unclear whether such an amendment exists or was legitimately adopted through ordinary legislative procedure.
- It is unclear whether Article 111(2)/113 cross-references have been formally updated to point to 2 December 2027 rather than 2 August 2026 following the Omnibus amendment.
- The full legal text of any "second amendment" allegedly agreed in September 2026 has not been located or verified.
- It remains unclear whether the 2 December 2027 date applies uniformly across all Annex III categories or whether sub-exceptions exist (e.g., under Article 6(5) reclassification mechanisms).
